title: The gift of use
hook: the gods gave us one thing wholly ours: the right use of impressions (Discourses 1.1)

segments.voice: Yesterday: a city called victory, and Arrian, the student writing down his teacher's very words. Your line was a real classroom. What did you read aloud? Day three hundred eighty-nine.

Spell-check can tell you a word is misspelled. It can't tell you whether to send the email. A music app can tell you the song is in the right key. It can't tell you whether this is the moment to sing it. Each tool judges its own work and goes quiet on the question of whether to use it. The very first discourse in the book opens with the same observation, using the tools of Epictetus' day. And then it asks: so what in us can answer the real question? Today: the gift of use.
screen: `SPELL-CHECK CAN'T TELL YOU TO SEND IT.` → `EVERY TOOL IS SILENT ABOUT SOMETHING.` → `THE GIFT OF USE.`

segments.voice: First, the tools. Look at all the skills and faculties, Epictetus says, and you won't find one that examines itself. Grammar can judge what's written, but if you're writing to a friend, grammar won't tell you whether to write. Music can judge a tune, but not whether to sing or play right now. Second, the one that does. What will tell you? The faculty that examines itself and everything else: reason. Only it asks what it is, what it can do, and what it's worth. Gold doesn't tell you gold is beautiful. Something in you does, by how it uses the impression of gold. Third, the gift. So the gods, Epictetus says, put in our power only the best thing, the ruler of all the rest: the right use of impressions. Everything else, they left outside our power. Then he imagines Zeus explaining himself. If I could have, Zeus says, I would have made your body and your little property free too. But your body isn't really yours. It's clay, cleverly mixed. Since I couldn't, I gave you a part of myself: this power to choose and refuse, to desire and avoid, to use impressions. Look after it, and you'll never be blocked. Fourth, why it matters. You might believe in Zeus, in God, in nature, in evolution, or in none of these, and Epictetus' point still lands. You didn't get to choose most of what happens. You did get one thing that's wholly yours: what you do with how things appear to you. An impression arrives: they're ignoring me. You get to examine it before you agree. That's the gift. And it's yours by use, not by owning it.
screen: `GRAMMAR CAN'T SAY WHETHER TO WRITE.` · `ONLY REASON EXAMINES ITSELF.` · `THE RIGHT USE OF IMPRESSIONS.` · `ZEUS: I GAVE YOU A PART OF MYSELF.` · then, large: `THE GIFT OF USE.`

segments.voice: Settle, and breathe. Let the sounds of the room come to you: a car, a fan, a voice next door. Almost at once, a comment arrives with each one: annoying, nice, too loud. You didn't choose the sound. The comment is an impression, and that's where the gift lives. For each sound, just notice two things: the sound, and then my take on it. You don't have to change the take. Seeing it as a take is the use. The bell holds the time.
The gift of use. Discourses one, chapter one: the one thing wholly ours is the right use of impressions. Today's word.
Your line: the gift of use. Use one impression well today: when a strong one arrives, look at it before you agree. Day three hundred eighty-nine.

howItsDone: People practicing Stoicism often pause on a strong first impression, such as an insult or a fear, and examine whether it is true before acting on it, which Epictetus calls the right use of impressions.

original.note: Greek: an impression or appearance, what the mind is given to use well.

trapdoor: what you thought: control your thoughts.
what it means: you can't choose what appears to you, but you can examine it before you agree, and that use is wholly yours.
what a scholar hears: chrēsis phantasiōn, the use of impressions, framed in Discourses 1.1 as Zeus's gift of a part of himself.

notes: Discourses 1.1 paraphrased: no art contemplates itself; grammar and music; the rational faculty contemplates itself and others; gold; the gods put in our power only the right use of appearances; Zeus: 'if it were possible I would have made your body and property free... it is clay cleverly mixed... I have given you a portion of ourselves, the faculty of pursuit and avoidance, desire and aversion, the use of appearances'. Confirm sections and sense.
Greek φαντασία and the phrase χρῆσις φαντασιῶν: confirm.
